clue.text: Catch tendency with book coming out to face criticism

indicators.note: the book abbreviation leaves the word for tendency, so its letter is taken away

parts.note: a bent is a natural inclination or tendency
rap is informal for a rebuke or criticism, as in a rap on the knuckles

explanation.surface: A habit of mind, once published, has to face the critics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming out' works on the tendency word, not on the book; 'to face' just puts the first piece in front of the criticism.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch someone out is to ensnare or trick them, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Deny appeal in North American yards

parts.note: N is the compass abbreviation for north

indicators.note: the appeal letters sit inside the pair of yard abbreviations

parts.note: Y is the abbreviation for yard, doubled for the plural
SA is short for sex appeal

explanation.surface: An appeal is turned down somewhere in North American backyards.
explanation.definitionFit: To gainsay is to deny or contradict, the same sense as refusing or opposing.

clue.text: Man in back with a lot of wit making preparation in house?

indicators.note: the man's pronoun goes inside the word for back

parts.note: the rear is the back
he is the pronoun for a man

indicators.note: most but not all of the word for wit, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: salt means pungent wit, as in Attic salt

explanation.surface: A fellow at the back with sharp wit getting ready at home.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'house' is a theatre: the run-through happens before an audience fills it, and the question mark admits the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: A run-through of a play before opening is the preparation done in a theatre, the question mark flagging the playhouse sense.

clue.text: One detained to bear awkwardly sporting vessel

parts.note: a POW is a prisoner of war, someone detained

indicators.note: done awkwardly suggests the letters are clumsily rearranged

explanation.surface: A prisoner is made to bear something awkward aboard a racing boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkwardly' rearranges the letters of 'to bear' to follow the prisoner of war.
explanation.definitionFit: A fast motor boat used for racing is a craft for sport.

clue.text: Remain around untidy sack in rear

indicators.note: the word for remain wraps round the rearranged letters

parts.note: to bide is to remain or stay

indicators.note: an untidy sack has its letters jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone stays put round a messy sack at the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rear' looks like a verb (to bring up) but is the noun for bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: The posterior or bottom is a person's rear, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Parking area attracting scribbled note? It's pointedly offensive

parts.note: a bay is a marked space for parking

indicators.note: a note scribbled hastily has its letters thrown about

explanation.surface: A parking space draws a hurriedly written ticket, which is pointedly offensive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offensive' is the military sense: a weapon for attacking, with a point.
explanation.definitionFit: A blade fixed to a rifle is used for stabbing attacks, so it is offensive with a point.

clue.text: Constant mass of logs in ship

parts.note: c is the scientific symbol for a constant such as the speed of light
a raft is logs lashed together into a floating platform

explanation.surface: A steady pile of timber floats in a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat or vessel of any kind is a seagoing craft.

clue.text: Stunted growth in twelfth man taking in opening pair in cricket

indicators.note: the substitute word takes the opening letters inside it

parts.note: in cricket the twelfth man is the substitute, a sub

indicators.note: the first two letters of the word cricket are taken

explanation.surface: The cricket reserve brings in the opening batsmen among stunted plants.
explanation.walkthrough: SUB takes in CR, the opening pair of letters of 'cricket'. A twelfth man is a cricket team's substitute fielder.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrub is low, stunted vegetation or brushwood.

clue.text: Fine fellow with revolutionary party in parliament producing national symbol

indicators.note: the fine, fellow and party letters go inside the parliament word

parts.note: the Dail is the lower house of the Irish parliament
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned round, so the party word is read backwards

parts.note: a do is a party

explanation.surface: A good chap and a rebel party sit in parliament, producing a national emblem.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dail is the Irish parliament. The answer is the national flower of Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: The yellow spring flower is a national emblem of Wales, worn on St David's Day.

clue.text: Spooner's question about horse incidentally

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so these sounds trade places

parts.note: why is a question word
a bay is a reddish-brown horse

explanation.surface: Someone asks what a horse is doing there, as an aside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Why the bay?' is a question about a horse; swap the W and B sounds and you get 'bye the way'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom introducing a passing remark means the same as incidentally.

clue.text: A disagreement about democrat going off course

parts.note: a rift is a breach or disagreement

explanation.surface: A political quarrel involving a Democrat sends things off course.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat drifting without control has lost its course, so it is wandering off track.

clue.text: Militant Arab defending extreme characters in marketplace

indicators.note: the rearranged letters surround and so protect the other piece
a militant Arab is a stirred-up one, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: Z and A are the alphabet's end and start, its extremes

explanation.surface: A fighter shields people at the extremes in a market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Militant' rearranges ARAB to BAAR, which surrounds ZA.
explanation.definitionFit: An oriental market or a sale of goods for charity is a marketplace.

clue.text: Statement of one rejecting a Kindle in jotting resource

definitions.text: Statement of one rejecting a Kindle
definitions.meaning: someone refusing Amazon's electronic reader might declare '...'
a pad of paper for making notes

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as NOT E-BOOK and it is what a lover of paper says about a Kindle.
explanation.definitionFit: A bound pad for writing notes is the resource used for jotting things down.

clue.text: Attention gripped by consummate artist

indicators.note: the letters are held within the run of the words consummate artist

explanation.surface: A perfect artist captures attention.
explanation.definitionFit: To lend an ear is to listen, so the word means attention or heed.

clue.text: Electrical problem, type besetting hotel and venues frequented by performers

indicators.note: the type word surrounds the hotel letter

parts.note: sort means type or kind
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a circuit is the round of venues that touring performers play

explanation.surface: Fuse trouble strikes a kind of hotel and the touring venues.
explanation.definitionFit: An unintended low-resistance connection causing a fault is a common electrical problem.

clue.text: Element beginning to engage in train disorganised traveller

indicators.note: disorganised means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: tin is a chemical element

indicators.note: only the first letter of engage is taken

explanation.surface: A chemical element begins to engage in a messy railway trip.
explanation.walkthrough: TIN, E and TRAIN together are rearranged by 'disorganised'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who travels from place to place is itinerant, used here as a noun.

clue.text: Charm in international footballer supported by tax in match

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits above the rest

parts.note: a cap is a player chosen for a national team

indicators.note: the tax word goes inside the match word

parts.note: a tie is a cup match
VAT is value added tax

explanation.surface: An international footballer, held up by tax, charms everyone in a match.
explanation.definitionFit: To captivate is to enthral or bewitch, a verb matching charm.

clue.text: Skip a lot of free decorative work with no end of flair

indicators.note: most of the word for free, losing its last letter

parts.note: to be rid of something is to be free of it

indicators.note: the craft word loses a letter

parts.note: crochet is decorative hooked needlework

indicators.note: the last letter of flair is the one removed

explanation.surface: Ornamental needlework lacking flair skips about.
explanation.walkthrough: RI is RID less D; CROCHET without R, the end of 'flair', is COCHET.
explanation.definitionFit: A stone that ricochets skips off a surface and bounces on.

clue.text: Elusive figure while plot is devised to trap wife

indicators.note: the anagram letters close round the wife letter
something devised is worked out anew, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A scheme is hatched to ensnare a wife, though she remains elusive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' belongs to the anagram fodder; 'devised' alone is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A will-o'-the-wisp is a phantom light, and by extension anyone or anything hard to catch.

clue.text: Approval to retain a tree

indicators.note: the approval word keeps the letter A held inside it

parts.note: OK signals approval

explanation.surface: Permission is needed to keep a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The oak is a familiar broadleaf tree of the genus Quercus.

clue.text: European singer wearing surprised expression in diplomatic venue

indicators.note: the expression is worn around the singer, so it encloses him

parts.note: 'my!' is an exclamation of surprise
a bass is a singer with the lowest voice

explanation.surface: A European vocalist with a startled face at the diplomatic residence.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambassador's official residence or office is a venue for diplomacy.

clue.text: Native American in South Dakota producing extensive text

indicators.note: the people's name is placed within the state abbreviation

parts.note: SD is the postal abbreviation for South Dakota
the Cree are a Native American people

explanation.surface: A Native American in South Dakota writes at length.
explanation.definitionFit: A screed is a long, often tedious piece of writing.

clue.text: Sound of bird trailed by wealthy figure — feature of an entrance?

indicators.note: the pair of words is spoken and heard as the answer

parts.note: a daw (jackdaw) followed by a nob, a wealthy toff, gives the words said aloud

explanation.surface: A bird's call is followed by a rich man at the front door.
explanation.walkthrough: Said in a non-rhotic British accent, 'daw nob' sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The handle turned to open a door is a fixture of an entrance, the question mark marking an example.

clue.text: Curtailed drink after port and wine

indicators.note: the drink piece comes after the port

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a major Brazilian port

indicators.note: curtailed means its tail is cut, so the final letter goes

parts.note: a jar is British slang for a drink, usually of beer

explanation.surface: A short drink after port, followed by some wine.
explanation.walkthrough: JAR loses its tail (R) to give JA.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioja is a red wine from the Spanish region of that name.

clue.text: Reminder front of gallery's enthralled by artistic model

indicators.note: held captive by, so the model word encloses the letter

parts.note: a nude is an unclothed model posing for artists

indicators.note: the first letter of the word gallery

explanation.surface: The front of a gallery is captivated by a model for a painting.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentle prod to remind someone is a nudge.

clue.text: Show clearly name in internet scam?

parts.note: e- is the prefix for internet or electronic

indicators.note: the name letter goes inside the scam word

parts.note: vice here stands for a criminal racket, as in a vice ring

explanation.surface: A name crops up in an online fraud, showing it plainly.
explanation.definitionFit: To evince a feeling is to display or reveal it plainly.

clue.text: Cover pair returning after small period of time

indicators.note: the reversed pair comes after the other pieces

parts.note: HR is short for hour

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the pair word reads backwards

parts.note: a duo is a pair

explanation.surface: A couple come back after a short time to cover something.
explanation.definitionFit: A shroud is a cloth wrapping, hence anything that covers.

clue.text: Rating maybe a food featured in series

indicators.note: these pieces appear inside the series abbreviation

parts.note: fare is food

explanation.surface: A rating features a type of food in a series.
explanation.walkthrough: A rating is a navy sailor below officer rank, not a score.
explanation.definitionFit: A rating, a navy ordinary seaman, is an example of a sailor, hence 'maybe'.

clue.text: Long-term plan from restaurant say in case of stringency

indicators.note: the restaurant and say pieces go inside the outer letters
the case is the outside, so only the first and last letters of stringency

parts.note: trat is short for trattoria, an Italian restaurant
EG, for example, is what 'say' means

explanation.surface: A long-term plan from a restaurant, for example, in tight times.
explanation.walkthrough: S and Y, the case of 'stringency', hold TRAT and EG.
explanation.definitionFit: A strategy is an overall plan of action for the long run.

clue.text: Hear about ambition that's fashionable

indicators.note: the hearing word goes round the ambition word

parts.note: to hear a case in court is to try it
an end is an aim or ambition

explanation.surface: Listen to talk of ambition that's in fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hear' is a judge hearing a case, not listening.
explanation.definitionFit: Being trendy is following the latest style, the same as being in vogue.
